title: Zachary's song (Luke 1:57–80)
hookLine: his tongue loosed, he sings of the dayspring from on high, prayed every morning

lines: NOBODY IN YOUR FAMILY IS JOHN.
cards: Elizabeth gives birth to a son, and the neighbors and relatives come to rejoice with her. On the eighth day they gather for his circumcision and naming, and they've already decided: he'll be Zachary, after his father.
Elizabeth says no. He shall be called John. But nobody in your family has that name, they say.
So they turn to the father, still mute after all these months, and make signs. Zachary asks for a writing tablet. Everyone leans in.
He writes four words: "John is his name."

teach.b: Immediately, Luke says, his mouth is opened and his tongue loosed, and he speaks, blessing God. The silence ends with obedience: he names the child the way the angel said.
And what comes out of him, filled with the Holy Ghost, is a song, called the Benedictus after its first word in Latin.

teach.h: BLESSED BE THE LORD GOD OF ISRAEL.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people." The first half looks back: the house of David, the prophets, the oath God swore to Abraham.
Then he turns to the baby: and thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest, to go before the face of the Lord and prepare his ways. Then the image the carry comes from.
The King James says: "the dayspring from on high hath visited us."
The Douay says: "the Orient from on high hath visited us: To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death; to direct our feet into the way of peace."

Dayspring and Orient both try to catch one Greek word, anatole: the rising of the sun, the place in the sky where light comes up. Christians hear in it Christ pictured as sunrise, coming to people sitting in the dark.
So the Church sets this song at dawn: in the Liturgy of the Hours it's sung every morning at Lauds, Morning Prayer.

teach.h: TO DIRECT OUR FEET INTO THE WAY OF PEACE.
teach.b: Months of silence, and the song that broke them became the Church's morning song.

how: The Benedictus, Zachary's canticle, is prayed every morning at Lauds (Morning Prayer) in the Liturgy of the Hours by priests and religious, and by lay Catholics who pray the Hours.

o: Latin for good speech, a Roman word for a sermon
Latin for blessed, the first word of Zachary's song
Latin for a blessing a priest gives at the end of Mass

p: where the Church sings it daily

s: the relatives wanted to name the baby Zachary
after his father. Elizabeth said John, and Zachary wrote it down.
the Douay and the King James use the same word for the dayspring
the King James has dayspring; the Douay has Orient. both translate anatole, the sunrise.
the Benedictus is prayed only at Christmas
it's prayed every morning at Lauds, Morning Prayer, all year.

games.q: you're Zachary, mute for months. your relatives want to name your son after you. they hand you a tablet. what do you write?
games.why: "John is his name." and immediately his mouth was opened, and he spoke, blessing God.

practice: Picture tomorrow's first light: the gray before dawn, then a line of gold at the window.
Choose one phrase from the song to meet it, the dayspring from on high, to enlighten them that sit in darkness, or to direct our feet into the way of peace, and say it over slowly until it's yours.
If you pray, it becomes a prayer; if not, let it be a way of greeting the light.

wordCard.voice: Benedictus. Latin for blessed, the first word of Zachary's song when his tongue was loosed, prayed by the Church every morning. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: rising, dawn, the east; translated dayspring (King James) and Orient (Douay) in Luke 1:78.

carryVoice: Your line: the dayspring from on high. Light, coming up over people sitting in the dark. Day four hundred forty-five, done.
